newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.

text.p: A total 44,500 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 45.902 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
Out of this, traders in France received 21,500 tonnes, in Belgium 11,000, in Denmark 6,000, in the U.K. 4,000 and in Germany 2,000 tonnes, it added.

This week's award brings the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 1.299 million tonnes. This compares with the 21,000 tonnes awarded on January 4, 1996, when the cumulative tonnage totalled 1.386 million tonnes.
Earlier on Wednesday, London traders had expected the subsidy for the current season whites campaign for licences to be 45.894 Ecus per 100 kilos.
Traders had also forecast Wednesday's total authorised sugar tonnage export awards to be a maximum 60,000 tonnes versus 40,500 in the last tender when the restitution was 46.316 Ecus.
